## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="x05-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- x05-ideas:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<dl class="lx-ideas"><dt>A capital stack</dt><dd>A big project's money comes in layers: senior debt, tax equity, the sponsor's own equity and sometimes a grant.</dd><dt>Order of payment</dt><dd>Cash pays operating costs, then the loan, then tax equity, then the sponsor; the sponsor is paid last and loses first.</dd><dt>Coverage</dt><dd>A lender sizes the loan so the cash available for debt service covers each payment by a margin, the debt-service coverage ratio.</dd><dt>Why contracts matter</dt><dd>With the same expected revenue, this project supports $125.7M of debt fully contracted and $81.7M fully merchant.</dd><dt>Illustrative</dt><dd>One typical year in 2025 dollars, settings inside the dated ranges of NREL's 2025 ATB; no taxes, flips or reserves.</dd></dl>
<!-- x05-ideas:end -->
</div>
</div>
<!-- x05-stop:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-card xs-stop" id="x05-stop"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Where we stop</p><h3>This side topic stops at the capital stack</h3><p class="xs-stop-lede">Finance enters the course as who puts in money, who is paid first and why lenders value contracts; structuring deals is a profession of its own.</p><div class="xs-stop-cols"><div><h4 class="xs-h">This side topic covers</h4><ul><li>The four layers of a capital stack and the order in which they are paid.</li><li>How a lender sizes a loan from cash flow and a coverage ratio.</li><li>Why contracted revenue supports more debt than revenue sold at market prices.</li></ul></div><div><h4 class="xs-h">Left to specialists</h4><ul><li>Structuring a deal: partnership flips, back-leverage, reserve accounts, term sheets.</li><li>Tax law, eligibility for credits and accounting standards.</li><li>Investment advice: this lesson rates no project and no investor.</li></ul></div></div><h4 class="xs-h">Read next, three rungs</h4><ol class="xs-ladder"><li><b>Start here.</b> Sections 4 and 6 walk through each source of capital, the debt-service coverage ratio and how financing changes a wind project's cost. <span class="xs-src"><a href="https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy17osti/68227.pdf">Schwabe, Feldman, Fields and Settle, Wind Energy Finance in the United States (NREL/TP-6A20-68227)</a>, August 2017</span></li><li><b>Go further.</b> The financing assumptions behind each technology's cost: interest rates, returns, coverage ratios and the tax-equity partnership. <span class="xs-src"><a href="https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/financial_cases_&amp;_methods">NLR, 2025 Electricity ATB, Financial Cases and Methods</a>, 2025 edition, read 7 November 2026</span></li><li><b>Go deep.</b> Build a project's cash flows with debt sizing and tax equity in a free model, with its financial documentation; then an introductory project-finance textbook. <span class="xs-src">NREL System Advisor Model (SAM), financial models documentation, cited by name; read 7 November 2026</span></li></ol></div>
<!-- x05-stop:end -->
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Sizing a loan, in symbols</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<!-- x05-deeper:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p>The lender's largest loan <var>D</var> ($), for a share <var>s</var> of the output sold under contract:</p><p class="x5-eq">D = A × [ s × CFADS ÷ DSCR<sub>c</sub> + (1 − s) × CFADS ÷ DSCR<sub>m</sub> ]</p><ul><li><b>CFADS</b>: cash available for debt service in a typical year, $ (revenue minus operating costs): $17.383M here.</li><li><b>DSCR<sub>c</sub>, DSCR<sub>m</sub></b>: the coverage the lender asks from contracted and from market cash, 1.30 and 2.00 (illustrative).</li><li><b>A</b> = (1 − (1 + r)<sup>−n</sup>) ÷ r: the loan, in $, that $1 a year repays at rate r over n years; at 6.5% and 15 years, A = 9.4027.</li></ul><p>Here CFADS × A = $17.383M × 9.4027 = $163.447M, the loan the whole cash could repay with no cushion. Fully contracted: ÷ 1.30 = $125.73M. Fully merchant: ÷ 2.00 = $81.72M.</p>
<!-- x05-deeper:end -->
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>What real deals add</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li><b>Energy cases.</b> Lenders test the loan against output that is beaten in 50%, 90% or 99% of years (P50, P90, P99), not one typical year (NREL, 2017, p. 18).</li>
<li><b>The flip.</b> In a partnership flip, tax equity takes most tax benefits and some cash until it reaches a set return, then the shares flip toward the sponsor (NREL, 2017, p. 22).</li>
<li><b>Back-leverage.</b> In recent wind deals the loan most often sat with the sponsor, secured on its share, so tax equity was paid ahead of it (NREL, 2017, pp. 17-18).</li>
<li><b>Short loans, long schedules.</b> Much wind term debt fell due after 5 to 7 years while being paid down as if longer, then was refinanced (NREL, 2017, p. 17).</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<p class="lx-lede">Two quick checks.</p>
<!-- x05-check:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="x05-myth"><div class="lx-qq" data-id="debtcost" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Debt is the most expensive money in a project's capital stack.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Debt is paid first and protected by collateral, so it asks the lowest return: the 2025 ATB assumes 6.5% for term debt and more for equity.</p></details></div></div><div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="x05"><div class="lx-qq" data-id="dscr" data-answer="b"><p class="lx-qtext">A project's cash available for debt service is $17.4M a year and its loan payment is $13.4M. What is its debt-service coverage ratio?</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">About 0.77</li><li data-value="b">About 1.30</li><li data-value="c">About 2.30</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$17.4M ÷ $13.4M = 1.30: the cash covers the payment 1.30 times. The ratio is cash over payment, not payment over cash (0.77).</p></details></div></div>
<!-- x05-check:end -->
```
